name: Osthol
description: Osthol , also known as osthole, is a naturally occurring coumarin compound isolated primarily from Cnidium monnieri and related plant sources. It is used across pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and nutraceutical formulations as a bioactive botanical ingredient. Identified by CAS 484-12-8 , this compound serves as an antioxidant stabilizer in various industrial applications. In personal care and cosmetic formulations, it is incorporated into scalp treatments and hair growth serums. Skin-conditioning products often utilize this botanical active as a key differentiator for high-end brands. Nutraceutical and dietary supplement manufacturers use it as a standardized plant extract ingredient in capsule and tablet formats. Pharmaceutical researchers and formulators source this material as a reference standard or active ingredient in preparations. Its antioxidant activity also supports use as a stabilizing agent in formulations sensitive to oxidative degradation. The material is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for easy integration into manufacturing processes. It is available in research-grade and high-purity specifications to meet diverse industry needs. HPLC purity levels typically range from 98% upward to meet strict pharmaceutical and analytical requirements. Standardized extract forms with defined content are also available for nutraceutical and cosmetic applications.
